speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start by assessing your neurological symptoms: Have you noticed any tremors, weakness, or changes in your coordination? Additionally, could you describe any visual disturbances, such as difficulty distinguishing colors or blurred vision?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That "drunk" appearance suggests significant ataxia. Does this gait instability worsen when you try to touch your nose with your finger or when you close your eyes? Also, have you noticed any changes in your vision, such as color blindness or blurred vision?

REQUEST TEST: Full neurological exam including finger-to-nose test and color vision assessment.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Finger-to-nose test shows evidence of ataxia with dysmetria; Color vision assessment: Normal.

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Patient
text: The walking difficulty and coordination problems are the main issues. I do not have chest pain or other major symptoms besides the neurological problems. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.
